name: Ski Trip Packing List
description: What to pack for a week on the mountain, from the layering system to the papers the rental shop will ask for.

items.text: 4-5 pairs of ski socks, tall enough to clear the boot cuff
items.note: One pair per day. Two pairs at once makes boots tighter and feet colder, not warmer.

items.text: No cotton anywhere in this layer
1 heavier insulated layer for cold days

items.note: One wet pair ends a day faster than almost anything else on this list.

items.text: Waterproof over-trousers if your shell is light
Sunglasses for the walk and the terrace
Skis, boots and poles, or a rental booking confirmation
Back protector if you ski off-piste
Small backpack for water, snacks and a spare layer
High-factor sunscreen for face and neck
items.note: Altitude and reflected snow burn skin far faster than the temperature suggests.

items.text: Swimwear for the hotel pool or spa
Passport and travel insurance covering winter sports
items.note: Standard travel policies routinely exclude skiing; check the wording rather than assuming.

items.text: EHIC/GHIC or equivalent health cover for the country
Lift pass booking or pass from a previous season
Rental booking, with height, weight and boot size noted
Resort and emergency numbers saved offline
Power bank — cold flattens phone batteries fast

faq.a: Three layers: a wicking merino or synthetic base layer, a fleece or light down mid layer, and a waterproof shell jacket and trousers. Avoid cotton at every level, because once it is damp it stops insulating and makes you colder for the rest of the day.

faq.q: Should I rent or bring my own skis?
faq.a: Rent, for most people. Ski carriage fees and the risk of damage in transit usually cost more than a week's rental, and rental shops service their skis between hires. Helmets and goggles are the exception — fit matters and they pack small.

faq.q: How many ski socks do I need?
faq.a: One tall pair per day, so four or five for a week. They must reach above the boot cuff, and a single pair is warmer than two: doubling up compresses the boot lining and cuts circulation.

faq.q: Does normal travel insurance cover skiing?
faq.a: Often not. Many standard policies exclude winter sports or charge extra for them, and off-piste skiing is usually excluded again on top. Read the policy wording before travelling rather than at the clinic.
